app_build.description: Internal build ID as it appears on the platform.

app_identifier.description: Version-independent application identifier, often a dotted bundle ID.

app_name.description: Application name as it appears on the platform.

app_start_time.description:
Start time of the app.

 Formatted UTC timestamp when the user started the application.

app_version.description: Application version as it appears on the platform.

build_type.description: String identifying the kind of build. For example, `testflight`.

in_foreground.description: A flag indicating whether the app is in foreground or not. An app is in foreground when it's visible to the user.

view_names.description: The names of the currently visible views.

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description:
Application information.

 App context describes the application. As opposed to the runtime, this is the actual
 application that was running and carries metadata about the current session.

name.description: Display name of the browser application.

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description: Web browser information.

arch.description: Native cpu architecture of the device.

battery_status.description:
Status of the device's battery.

 For example, `Unknown`, `Charging`, `Discharging`, `NotCharging`, `Full`.

boot_time.description: Indicator when the device was booted.

charging.description: Whether the device was charging or not.

cpu_description.description:
CPU description.

 For example, Intel(R) Core(TM)2 Quad CPU Q6600 @ 2.40GHz.

device_type.description:
Kind of device the application is running on.

 For example, `Unknown`, `Handheld`, `Console`, `Desktop`.

family.description:
Family of the device model.

 This is usually the common part of model names across generations. For instance, `iPhone`
 would be a reasonable family, so would be `Samsung Galaxy`.

locale.description: ISO 639-1 code of the locale the device is set to.

low_memory.description: Whether the device was low on memory.

model.description:
Device model.

 This, for example, can be `Samsung Galaxy S3`.

model_id.description:
Device model (internal identifier).

 An internal hardware revision to identify the device exactly.

name.description: Name of the device.

online.description: Whether the device was online or not.

orientation.description:
Current screen orientation.

 This can be a string `portrait` or `landscape` to define the orientation of a device.

supports_accelerometer.description: Whether the accelerometer is available on the device.

supports_audio.description: Whether audio is available on the device.

supports_gyroscope.description: Whether the gyroscope is available on the device.

supports_location_service.description: Whether location support is available on the device.

supports_vibration.description: Whether vibration is available on the device.

timezone.description: Timezone of the device.

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description:
Device information.

 Device context describes the device that caused the event. This is most appropriate for mobile
 applications.

api_type.description:
The device low-level API type.

 Examples: `"Apple Metal"` or `"Direct3D11"`

graphics_shader_level.description:
Approximate "shader capability" level of the graphics device.

 For Example: Shader Model 2.0, OpenGL ES 3.0, Metal / OpenGL ES 3.1, 27 (unknown)

id.description: The PCI identifier of the graphics device.

multi_threaded_rendering.description: Whether the GPU has multi-threaded rendering or not.

name.description: The name of the graphics device.

supports_compute_shaders.description: Whether compute shaders are available on the device.

supports_draw_call_instancing.description: Whether GPU draw call instancing is supported.

supports_geometry_shaders.description: Whether geometry shaders are available on the device.

supports_ray_tracing.description: Whether ray tracing is available on the device.

vendor_id.description: The PCI vendor identifier of the graphics device.

vendor_name.description: The vendor name as reported by the graphics device.

version.description: The Version of the graphics device.

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description:
GPU information.

 Example:

 ```json
 "gpu": {
   "name": "AMD Radeon Pro 560",
   "vendor_name": "Apple",
   "memory_size": 4096,
   "api_type": "Metal",
   "multi_threaded_rendering": true,
   "version": "Metal",
   "npot_support": "Full"
 }
 ```
Monitor information.

build.description: Internal build number of the operating system.

kernel_version.description:
Current kernel version.

 This is typically the entire output of the `uname` syscall.

name.description: Name of the operating system.

raw_description.description:
Unprocessed operating system info.

 An unprocessed description string obtained by the operating system. For some well-known
 runtimes, Sentry will attempt to parse `name` and `version` from this string, if they are
 not explicitly given.

rooted.description: Indicator if the OS is rooted (mobile mostly).

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description:
Operating system information.

 OS context describes the operating system on which the event was created. In web contexts, this
 is the operating system of the browser (generally pulled from the User-Agent string).

OpenTelemetry Context

 If an event has this context, it was generated from an OpenTelemetry signal (trace, metric, log).

build.description: Application build string, if it is separate from the version.

name.description: Runtime name.

raw_description.description:
Unprocessed runtime info.

 An unprocessed description string obtained by the runtime. For some well-known runtimes,
 Sentry will attempt to parse `name` and `version` from this string, if they are not
 explicitly given.

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description:
Runtime information.

 Runtime context describes a runtime in more detail. Typically, this context is present in
 `contexts` multiple times if multiple runtimes are involved (for instance, if you have a
 JavaScript application running on top of JVM).

origin.description: The origin of the trace indicates what created the trace (see [OriginType] docs).

sampled.description:
Track whether the trace connected to this event has been sampled entirely.

 This flag only applies to events with [`Error`] type that have an associated dynamic sampling context.

GetOrganizationIssueEvent200ResponseCont.description: Trace context

DataForwarderConfigProperty.description:
The configuration for the data forwarder, specific to the provider type. 
For a 'sqs' provider, the required keys are queue_url, region, access_key, secret_key. If using a FIFO queue, you must also provide a message_group_id, though s3_bucket is optional. 
For a 'segment' provider, the required keys are write_key. 
For a 'splunk' provider, the required keys are instance_url, index, source, token.

DetectorCreateRequestConfigProperty.description:
The issue detection type configuration.


            - `detectionType`
                - `static`: Threshold based monitor
                - `percent`: Change based monitor
                - `dynamic`: Dynamic monitor
            - `comparisonDelta`: If selecting a **change** detection type, the comparison delta is the time period, in seconds, at which to compare against historical data.
            For example, a value of 3600 compares the metric tracked against data 1 hour ago.
                - `300`: 5 minutes
                - `900`: 15 minutes
                - `3600`: 1 hour
                - `86400`: 1 day
                - `604800`: 1 week
                - `2592000`: 1 month

            **Threshold**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "static"
            }
            ```
            **Change**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "percent",
                "comparisonDelta": 3600
            }
            ```
            **Dynamic**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "dynamic"
            }
            ```

DetectorUpdateRequestConfigProperty.description:

            - `detectionType`

            - `comparisonDelta`: If selecting a **change** detection type, the comparison delta is the time period, in seconds, at which to compare against historical data.
            For example, a value of 3600 compares the metric tracked against data 1 hour ago.
                - `300`: 5 minutes
                - `900`: 15 minutes
                - `3600`: 1 hour
                - `86400`: 1 day
                - `604800`: 1 week
                - `2592000`: 1 month

            **Threshold**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "static"
            }
            ```
            **Change**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "percent",
                "comparisonDelta": 3600
            }
            ```
            **Dynamic**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "dynamic"
            }
            ```

UpdateOrganizationDetectorRequestConditi.description:
Issue detection configuration for when to create an issue and at what priority level.


            - `logicType`: `any`
            - `type`: Any of `gt` (greater than), `gte` (greater than or equal), `lt` (less than), `lte` (less than or equal), or `anomaly_detection` (dynamic)
            - `comparison`: Any positive integer. This is threshold that must be crossed for the monitor to create an issue, e.g. "Create a metric issue when there are more than 5 unresolved error events".
                - If creating a **change** monitor, `comparison` is the current value as a percentage of the value `comparisonDelta` seconds earlier, not the size of the change. For example, use `120` with `gt` for 20% higher, or `70` with `lt` for 30% lower.
                - If creating a **dynamic** monitor, see the options below.
                    - `seasonality`: `auto`
                    - `sensitivity`: Level of responsiveness. Options are one of `low`, `medium`, or `high`
                    - `thresholdType`: If you want to be alerted to anomalies that are moving above, below, or in both directions in relation to your threshold.
                        - `0`: Above
                        - `1`: Below
                        - `2`: Above and below

            - `conditionResult`: The issue state change when the threshold is crossed.
                - `75`: High priority
                - `50`: Low priority
                - `0`: Resolved


            **Threshold Monitor**
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        "type": "gt",
                        "comparison": 10,
                        "conditionResult": 75
                    },
                    {
                        "type": "lte",
                        "comparison": 10,
                        "conditionResult": 0
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            **Change Monitor** (20% higher than `comparisonDelta` seconds earlier)
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        "type": "gt",
                        "comparison": 120,
                        "conditionResult": 75
                    },
                    {
                        "type": "lte",
                        "comparison": 120,
                        "conditionResult": 0
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            **Threshold Monitor with Medium Priority**
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        type: "gt",
                        comparison: 5,
                        conditionResult: 75
                    },
                    {
                        type: "gt",
                        comparison: 2,
                        conditionResult: 50
                    },
                    {
                        type: "lte",
                        comparison: 2,
                        conditionResult: 0
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            **Dynamic Monitor**
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        "type": "anomaly_detection",
                        "comparison": {
                            "seasonality": "auto",
                            "sensitivity": "medium",
                            "thresholdType": 2
                        },
                        "conditionResult": 75
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            - `logicType`: `any`
            - `type`: Any of `gt` (greater than), `gte` (greater than or equal), `lt` (less than), `lte` (less than or equal), or `anomaly_detection` (dynamic)
            - `comparison`: Any positive integer. This is threshold that must be crossed for the monitor to create an issue, e.g. "Create a metric issue when there are more than 5 unresolved error events".
                - If creating a **change** monitor, `comparison` is the current value as a percentage of the value `comparisonDelta` seconds earlier, not the size of the change. For example, use `120` with `gt` for 20% higher, or `70` with `lt` for 30% lower.
                - If creating a **dynamic** monitor, see the options below.
                    - `seasonality`: `auto`
                    - `sensitivity`: Level of responsiveness. Options are one of `low`, `medium`, or `high`
                    - `thresholdType`: If you want to be alerted to anomalies that are moving above, below, or in both directions in relation to your threshold.
                        - `0`: Above
                        - `1`: Below
                        - `2`: Above and below

            - `conditionResult`: The issue state change when the threshold is crossed.
                - `75`: High priority
                - `50`: Low priority
                - `0`: Resolved


            **Threshold Monitor**
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        "type": "gt",
                        "comparison": 10,
                        "conditionResult": 75
                    },
                    {
                        "type": "lte",
                        "comparison": 10,
                        "conditionResult": 0
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            **Change Monitor** (20% higher than `comparisonDelta` seconds earlier)
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        "type": "gt",
                        "comparison": 120,
                        "conditionResult": 75
                    },
                    {
                        "type": "lte",
                        "comparison": 120,
                        "conditionResult": 0
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            **Threshold Monitor with Medium Priority**
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        type: "gt",
                        comparison: 5,
                        conditionResult: 75
                    },
                    {
                        type: "gt",
                        comparison: 2,
                        conditionResult: 50
                    },
                    {
                        type: "lte",
                        comparison: 2,
                        conditionResult: 0
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

            **Dynamic Monitor**
            ```json
                "logicType": "any",
                "conditions": [
                    {
                        "type": "anomaly_detection",
                        "comparison": {
                            "seasonality": "auto",
                            "sensitivity": "medium",
                            "thresholdType": 2
                        },
                        "conditionResult": 75
                    }
                ],
                "actions": []
            ```

CustomInboundFilterDataType.description:
The data the filter matches against. `all` is the catch-all: it filters every data type Sentry ingests, including ones added later, and accepts only the conditions that every data type carries a field for.

* `all`
* `error`
* `log`
* `metric`
* `span`

CustomInboundFilterConditionType.description:
The field the condition matches against. Every `dataType` accepts `release` and `ip_address`. In addition, `error` accepts `error_type`, `error_message` and `geo_country_code`, `log` accepts `log_message`, and `metric` accepts `metric_name`. `span` and `all` accept no other types.

* `error_type`
* `error_message`
* `log_message`
* `metric_name`
* `release`
* `ip_address`
* `geo_country_code`

CustomInboundFilterConditionOperator.description:
How the field compares to `value`. `glob` matches the field against each value as a glob pattern. `equals`, `starts_with`, `contains` and `ends_with` match the field against each value case-insensitively, with every character read literally; `does_not_start_with`, `does_not_contain` and `does_not_end_with` match when the field is set and no value does. `cidr` matches `ip_address` against each value as an address or a CIDR range, and `not_cidr` matches when no value does. `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte` compare one value as a version and only apply to `release`.

* `glob`
* `equals`
* `starts_with`
* `contains`
* `ends_with`
* `does_not_start_with`
* `does_not_contain`
* `does_not_end_with`
* `cidr`
* `not_cidr`
* `gt`
* `gte`
* `lt`
* `lte`

OrganizationMemberRequestOrgRole.description:
The organization-level role of the new member. Roles include:

* `billing` - Can manage payment and compliance details.
* `member` - Can view and act on events, as well as view most other data within the organization.
* `manager` - Has full management access to all teams and projects. Can also manage
        the organization's membership.
* `owner` - Has unrestricted access to the organization, its data, and its
        settings. Can add, modify, and delete projects and members, as well as
        make billing and plan changes.
* `admin` - Can edit global integrations, manage projects, and add/remove teams.
        They automatically assume the Team Admin role for teams they join.
        Note: This role can no longer be assigned in Business and Enterprise plans. Use `TeamRoles` instead.

OrganizationMemberTeamTeamRole.description:
The team-level role to switch to. Valid roles include:

* `contributor` - Contributors can view and act on events, as well as view most other data within the team's projects.
* `admin` - Admin privileges on the team. They can create and remove projects, and can manage the team's memberships.

name.description: Name of the monitor.

workflowIds.description: The IDs of the alerts to connect this monitor to. Use the 'Fetch Alerts' endpoint to find the IDs.

allOf.description:
The data sources for the metric monitor to use based on what you want to measure.

            The schema of each data source lists the `aggregate` values that its `dataset` and
            `eventTypes` accept.

            `timeWindow` is measured in seconds. Cron Monitors use schedules instead of this field.
            Legacy metric alert rules expressed this value in minutes, so multiply a legacy value
            by 60 when migrating it to a monitor. For example, a legacy 5-minute window becomes
            `"timeWindow": 300`.

            **Number of Errors Metric Monitor**
            - `eventTypes`: Any of `error` or `default`.
            ```json
                [
                    {
                        "aggregate": "count()",
                        "dataset" : "events",
                        "environment": "prod",
                        "eventTypes": ["default", "error"],
                        "query": "is:unresolved",
                        "queryType": 0,
                        "timeWindow": 3600
                    }
                ]
            ```

            **Users Experiencing Errors Metric Monitor**
            - `eventTypes`: Any of `error` or `default`.
            ```json
                [
                    {
                        "aggregate": "count_unique(tags[sentry:user])",
                        "dataset" : "events",
                        "environment": "prod",
                        "eventTypes": ["default", "error"],
                        "query": "is:unresolved",
                        "queryType": 0,
                        "timeWindow": 3600
                    }
                ]
            ```


            **Throughput Metric Monitor**
            ```json
                [
                    {
                        "aggregate":"count(span.duration)",
                        "dataset":"events_analytics_platform",
                        "environment":"prod",
                        "eventTypes":["trace_item_span"],
                        "query":"",
                        "queryType":1,
                        "timeWindow":3600,
                        "extrapolationMode":"unknown"
                    }
                ]
            ```

            **Duration Metric Monitor**
            ```json
                [
                    {
                        "aggregate":"p95(span.duration)",
                        "dataset":"events_analytics_platform",
                        "environment":"prod",
                        "eventTypes":["trace_item_span"],
                        "query":"",
                        "queryType":1,
                        "timeWindow":3600,
                        "extrapolationMode":"unknown"
                    }
                ]
            ```

            **Failure Rate Metric Monitor**
            ```json
                [
                    {
                        "aggregate":"failure_rate()",
                        "dataset":"events_analytics_platform",
                        "environment":"prod",
                        "eventTypes":["trace_item_span"],
                        "query":"",
                        "queryType":1,
                        "timeWindow":3600,
                        "extrapolationMode":"unknown"
                    }
                ]
            ```

            **Largest Contentful Paint Metric Monitor**
            - `dataset`: Use `events_analytics_platform`. To query transaction spans, add `is_transaction:true` to `query`.
            - `aggregate`: Valid values are `avg(measurements.lcp)`, `p50(measurements.lcp)`, `p75(measurements.lcp)`, `p95(measurements.lcp)`, `p99(measurements.lcp)`, and `p100(measurements.lcp)`.

            ```json
                [
                    {
                        "aggregate":"p95(measurements.lcp)",
                        "dataset":"events_analytics_platform",
                        "environment":"prod",
                        "eventTypes":["trace_item_span"],
                        "query":"is_transaction:true",
                        "queryType":1,
                        "timeWindow":3600,
                        "extrapolationMode":"unknown"
                    }
                ]
            ```

            **Custom Metric Monitor**
            - `dataset`: Use `events_analytics_platform`. To query transaction spans, add `is_transaction:true` to `query`.
            - `aggregate`: Valid values are:
            `avg(x)`, where `x` is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p50(x)`, where `x` is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p75(x)`, where x is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p95(x)`, where x is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p99(x)`, where x is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p100(x)`, where `x` is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `failure_rate()`
            `apdex(x)`, where `x` is the value of the Apdex score.
            `count()`

            ```json
            [
                {
                    "aggregate": "p75(measurements.ttfb)",
                    "dataset": "events_analytics_platform",
                    "environment": "prod",
                    "queryType": 1,
                    "eventTypes": ["trace_item_span"],
                    "query": "is_transaction:true",
                    "timeWindow": 3600,
                    "extrapolationMode": "unknown"
                }
            ]
            ```

config.description:
The issue detection type configuration.


            - `detectionType`
                - `static`: Threshold based monitor
                - `percent`: Change based monitor
                - `dynamic`: Dynamic monitor
            - `comparisonDelta`: If selecting a **change** detection type, the comparison delta is the time period, in seconds, at which to compare against historical data.
            For example, a value of 3600 compares the metric tracked against data 1 hour ago.
                - `300`: 5 minutes
                - `900`: 15 minutes
                - `3600`: 1 hour
                - `86400`: 1 day
                - `604800`: 1 week
                - `2592000`: 1 month

            **Threshold**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "static"
            }
            ```
            **Change**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "percent",
                "comparisonDelta": 3600
            }
            ```
            **Dynamic**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "dynamic"
            }
            ```

config.description:
The issue detection type configuration.


            - `detectionType`
                - `static`: Threshold based monitor
                - `percent`: Change based monitor
                - `dynamic`: Dynamic monitor
            - `comparisonDelta`: If selecting a **change** detection type, the comparison delta is the time period, in seconds, at which to compare against historical data.
            For example, a value of 3600 compares the metric tracked against data 1 hour ago.
                - `300`: 5 minutes
                - `900`: 15 minutes
                - `3600`: 1 hour
                - `86400`: 1 day
                - `604800`: 1 week
                - `2592000`: 1 month

            **Threshold**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "static"
            }
            ```
            **Change**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "percent",
                "comparisonDelta": 3600
            }
            ```
            **Dynamic**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "dynamic"
            }
            ```

config.description:
The issue detection type configuration.


            - `detectionType`
                - `static`: Threshold based monitor
                - `percent`: Change based monitor
                - `dynamic`: Dynamic monitor
            - `comparisonDelta`: If selecting a **change** detection type, the comparison delta is the time period, in seconds, at which to compare against historical data.
            For example, a value of 3600 compares the metric tracked against data 1 hour ago.
                - `300`: 5 minutes
                - `900`: 15 minutes
                - `3600`: 1 hour
                - `86400`: 1 day
                - `604800`: 1 week
                - `2592000`: 1 month

            **Threshold**
            ```json

                "detectionType": "static"
            }
            ```
            **Change**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "percent",
                "comparisonDelta": 3600
            }
            ```

                "detectionType": "dynamic"
            }
            ```

config.description:
The issue detection type configuration.


            - `detectionType`
                - `static`: Threshold based monitor
                - `percent`: Change based monitor
                - `dynamic`: Dynamic monitor
            - `comparisonDelta`: If selecting a **change** detection type, the comparison delta is the time period, in seconds, at which to compare against historical data.
            For example, a value of 3600 compares the metric tracked against data 1 hour ago.
                - `300`: 5 minutes
                - `900`: 15 minutes
                - `3600`: 1 hour
                - `86400`: 1 day
                - `604800`: 1 week
                - `2592000`: 1 month

            **Threshold**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "static"
            }
            ```
            **Change**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "percent",
                "comparisonDelta": 3600
            }
            ```
            **Dynamic**
            ```json
            {
                "detectionType": "dynamic"
            }
            ```

            `p50(x)`, where `x` is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p75(x)`, where x is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p95(x)`, where x is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p99(x)`, where x is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `p100(x)`, where `x` is `transaction.duration`, `measurements.cls`, `measurements.fcp`, `measurements.fid`, `measurements.fp`, `measurements.lcp`, `measurements.ttfb`, or `measurements.ttfb.requesttime`.
            `failure_rate()`
            `apdex(x)`, where `x` is the value of the Apdex score.
            `count()`

            ```json
            [
                {
                    "aggregate": "p75(measurements.ttfb)",
                    "dataset": "events_analytics_platform",
                    "environment": "prod",
                    "queryType": 1,
                    "eventTypes": ["trace_item_span"],
                    "query": "is_transaction:true",
                    "timeWindow": 3600,
                    "extrapolationMode": "unknown"
                }
            ]
            ```

The ID user or team who owns the monitor or alert prefaced by the string 'user' or 'team'.

            **User**
            ```json
                "user:123456"
            ```

            **Team**
            ```json
                "team:456789"
            ```

app_name.description: Application name as it appears on the platform.

app_start_time.description:

app_version.description: Application version as it appears on the platform.

build_type.description: String identifying the kind of build. For example, `testflight`.

in_foreground.description: A flag indicating whether the app is in foreground or not. An app is in foreground when it's visible to the user.

view_names.description: The names of the currently visible views.

arch.description: Native cpu architecture of the device.

battery_status.description:
Status of the device's battery.

boot_time.description: Indicator when the device was booted.

charging.description: Whether the device was charging or not.

cpu_description.description:
CPU description.

device_type.description:

family.description:

locale.description: ISO 639-1 code of the locale the device is set to.

low_memory.description: Whether the device was low on memory.

model.description:

online.description: Whether the device was online or not.

 This, for example, can be `Samsung Galaxy S3`.

model_id.description:
Device model (internal identifier).

 An internal hardware revision to identify the device exactly.

name.description: Name of the device.

online.description: Whether the device was online or not.

orientation.description:
Current screen orientation.

 This can be a string `portrait` or `landscape` to define the orientation of a device.

supports_accelerometer.description: Whether the accelerometer is available on the device.

supports_audio.description: Whether audio is available on the device.

supports_gyroscope.description: Whether the gyroscope is available on the device.

supports_location_service.description: Whether location support is available on the device.

supports_vibration.description: Whether vibration is available on the device.

timezone.description: Timezone of the device.

allOf.description:
Device information.

 Device context describes the device that caused the event. This is most appropriate for mobile
 applications.

api_type.description:
The device low-level API type.

 Examples: `"Apple Metal"` or `"Direct3D11"`

graphics_shader_level.description:
Approximate "shader capability" level of the graphics device.

 For Example: Shader Model 2.0, OpenGL ES 3.0, Metal / OpenGL ES 3.1, 27 (unknown)

id.description: The PCI identifier of the graphics device.

multi_threaded_rendering.description: Whether the GPU has multi-threaded rendering or not.

name.description: The name of the graphics device.

supports_compute_shaders.description: Whether compute shaders are available on the device.

supports_draw_call_instancing.description: Whether GPU draw call instancing is supported.

supports_geometry_shaders.description: Whether geometry shaders are available on the device.

supports_ray_tracing.description: Whether ray tracing is available on the device.

vendor_id.description: The PCI vendor identifier of the graphics device.

vendor_name.description: The vendor name as reported by the graphics device.

version.description: The Version of the graphics device.

allOf.description:
GPU information.

 Example:

 ```json
 "gpu": {
   "name": "AMD Radeon Pro 560",
   "vendor_name": "Apple",
   "memory_size": 4096,
   "api_type": "Metal",
   "multi_threaded_rendering": true,
   "version": "Metal",
   "npot_support": "Full"
 }
 ```

build.description: Internal build number of the operating system.

kernel_version.description:
Current kernel version.

 This is typically the entire output of the `uname` syscall.

name.description: Name of the operating system.

raw_description.description:
Unprocessed operating system info.

 An unprocessed description string obtained by the operating system. For some well-known
 runtimes, Sentry will attempt to parse `name` and `version` from this string, if they are
 not explicitly given.

rooted.description: Indicator if the OS is rooted (mobile mostly).

allOf.description:
Operating system information.

 OS context describes the operating system on which the event was created. In web contexts, this
 is the operating system of the browser (generally pulled from the User-Agent string).

OpenTelemetry Context

 If an event has this context, it was generated from an OpenTelemetry signal (trace, metric, log).

origin.description: The origin of the trace indicates what created the trace (see [OriginType] docs).
